title: Continuous integral matrices of locally constant module type admit local Smith forms
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and its valuation topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and choose a uniformizer $\pi\in A$ (a generator of its maximal ideal). Let $Y$ be any topological space, let $m,n\geq0$ be integers, and let $F:Y\to\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(A)$ have continuous entries. For $y\in Y$ put $P_y=A^n/F(y)(A^m)$, an ordinary scalar $A$-module. Suppose the isomorphism class of $P_y$ is locally constant: every $y$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ such that $P_z\cong P_y$ as $A$-modules for all $z\in W$. Then $Y$ has an open covering $(W_\alpha)$ on each member of which there are entrywise continuous invertible matrices $L_\alpha:W_\alpha\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ and $R_\alpha:W_\alpha\to\operatorname{GL}_m(A)$, with entrywise continuous inverses, and a fixed rectangular diagonal matrix $D_\alpha$ such that
$$L_\alpha(z)F(z)R_\alpha(z)=D_\alpha\quad(z\in W_\alpha).$$
Here $\operatorname{GL}_q(A)$ means the invertible $q\times q$ matrices, and the nonzero diagonal entries of $D_\alpha$ are $\pi^{e_1},\ldots,\pi^{e_r}$ for integers $0\leq e_1\leq\cdots\leq e_r$ and $r\leq\min(m,n)$; every other entry is zero. Empty matrices and $r=0$ are included. No scheme, sheaf, Noetherianity, or extremal disconnectedness hypothesis on $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Example 3.1 and the continuous integral pivot/division argument in the proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite E case. Agent local constant-type Smith variant, not a theorem quoted verbatim from HRS; the argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: At a point choose the open constant-cokernel neighbourhood. Apply rectangular scalar Smith form to the central matrix. Equality of cokernel finranks and the quotient-plus-range finrank formula show equality of the matrix ranks on this neighbourhood. Conjugate the family by the constant scalar Smith factors.

The conjugated family equals the chosen diagonal at the centre and has rank at most its number of pivots. Apply fixed-diagonal rank-locus reduction. Transport the resulting neighbourhood through the open subtype inclusion and compose its continuous factors with the constant scalar Smith factors; continuity of inverse entries follows by reversing multiplication.
Choose the constructed neighbourhood and factors at every point to get the point-indexed open cover.

proof_origin.place: Scalar Smith form, rank invariance of cokernels, and local diagonal rank-locus reduction.
